reports.note: Broadcast media reports a tornado east of Seminole around 6 PM CST.
An EF-0 tornado with max wind speed of 85 mph and a path width of 25 yards began at this location. The tornado tracked for 1.10 miles and impacted a barn and RV.

An EF-1 tornado began along Old York Road. First noticeable damage was a farm building approximately 3/4 of a mile southwest of the Old York Road and Bordentown Chesterfield Road intersection. All external walls of that building had collapsed. Additional tree damage was noted in multiple locations along Old York Road ahead of the intersection with Bordentown Chesterfield Road. Northeast of the intersection, still along Old York Road, a residence lost a significant portion of the roof over the front of the house. From this point, the tornado continued along a path parallel to Bordentown Chesterfield Road. A school along here lost roof covering and farm equipment nearby was overturned. Some tree damage just beyond the school was the last damage in the continuous path. Estimated maximum wind speed was 100 mph. The total path length was 1.5 miles, and maximum path width was 100 yards.

A brief tornado destroyed a metal outbuilding and some fencing west of Highway 137 and south of County Road 14. A tree was snapped and a couple of trailers were tossed. The tornado lasted approximately a minute.

On the afternoon of November 12th, an EF-1 tornado occurred on the eastern side of Newark, in New Castle County, Delaware. The tornado began in the southern portion of the Salem Woods neighborhood traveling to the north-northeast, primarily damaging siding and removing shingles from several houses, as well as uprooting and breaking large branches from a few trees. As the tornado approached White Drive, it began to wrap to the north-northwest, while continuing to produce minor damage to houses along the way. The initial circulation may have briefly lifted here before it touched down again and continued to the northeast where it exited Salem Woods and crossed Old Baltimore Pike into The Oaks neighborhood. Here, more minor roof and siding damage was observed. As the tornado then entered the Timber Farms neighborhood, it likely wrapped up briefly once again near the intersection of Hummock Lane and Marie Court.
